issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) requires the Animal name getter and setter to have protected visibility, but the Solution implements getName() and setName() as public. This contradicts the specified encapsulation and could confuse students about the intended visibility and inheritance usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal.getName() and Animal.setName() methods protected to match the UML and problem description (change their visibility from public to protected). Update any references accordingly so subclasses can access them while external classes cannot.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement indicates the Animal(String) constructor should be protected (shown with '#'), but the Solution implements this constructor as public. This is a visibility mismatch between the design diagram and the provided implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Animal constructor visibility to protected (protected Animal(String name)) to follow the UML design, preventing direct instantiation outside the inheritance hierarchy while allowing subclasses to call the constructor.
